<div class="container">
    

    <div class="guide-header">
        <span class="ai-badge"><i class="fas fa-clipboard-check"></i> Compliance & Governance</span>
        <h1>The 2026 Compliance Checklist: DORA, EU AI Act & NIST Mastery</h1>
        <p style="color:var(--text-muted);font-size:1.1rem;">Comprehensive cheat sheet for navigating 2026's
            regulatory landscape</p>
        <div style="margin-top:1rem;color:var(--text-muted);">
            <span><i class="fas fa-book-open"></i> 22 min read</span> <span style="margin:0 0.5rem;">|</span>
            <span><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Intermediate</span> <span style="margin:0 0.5rem;">|</span>
            <span><i class="far fa-calendar-alt"></i> January 2026</span>
        </div>
    </div>

    <img src="/images/guides/compliance-checklist-2026.png" alt="2026 Compliance Checklist Guide"
        class="featured-image"
        style="width:100%;max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:12px;margin:2rem 0;box-shadow:0 10px 40px rgba(16,185,129,0.2);border:1px solid var(--border);" loading="lazy">

    <div class="deadline-box" style="margin-bottom:2rem;">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-clock"></i> Critical Deadlines:</strong>
        <ul style="margin-top:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0;">
            <li><strong>DORA:</strong> Full enforcement since January 17, 2025 — audits ongoing</li>
            <li><strong>EU AI Act (High-Risk):</strong> August 2, 2026 — 6 months remaining</li>
            <li><strong>NIST CSF 2.0:</strong> Voluntary but increasingly expected by regulators</li>
        </ul>
    </div>

    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-file-alt"></i> Abstract:</strong>
        2026 marks a critical inflection point in cybersecurity regulation. Financial services organizations must
        demonstrate DORA compliance under active regulatory scrutiny. AI deployers face EU AI Act obligations for
        high-risk systems. NIST CSF 2.0's new GOVERN function has become the de facto standard for board-level risk
        reporting. This guide provides actionable checklists for each framework, identifies overlapping controls to
        reduce duplication, and offers audit preparation strategies. Target audience: CISOs, GRC managers,
        compliance officers, and security managers preparing for regulatory assessments.
    </div>

    <div class="toc">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-list-ul"></i> Table of Contents</h3>
        <ul>
            <li><a href="#overview">1. 2026 Regulatory Landscape Overview</a></li>

            <li><a href="#nist">4. NIST CSF 2.0 Quick Reference</a></li>
            <li><a href="#mapping">5. Control Mapping: One Effort, Three Frameworks</a></li>
            <li><a href="#audit">6. Audit Preparation Strategies</a></li>
            <li><a href="#tools">7. Compliance Automation Tools</a></li>
            <li><a href="#references">8. References</a></li>
        </ul>

    <h2 id="overview">1. 2026 Regulatory Landscape Overview</h2>

    <p>The convergence of cybersecurity, operational resilience, and AI governance regulations creates both
        challenges and opportunities for organizations. Understanding the scope and interactions between frameworks
        is essential.</p>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Framework</th>
                <th>Scope</th>
                <th>Key Deadline</th>
                <th>Penalty Risk</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><span class="framework-badge badge-dora">DORA</span> Digital Operational Resilience Act</td>
                <td>EU financial entities + ICT providers</td>
                <td>Active enforcement</td>
                <td>Up to 2% global turnover</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><span class="framework-badge badge-euai">EU AI Act</span></td>
                <td>AI systems deployed/developed in EU</td>
                <td>Aug 2, 2026 (high-risk)</td>
                <td>Up to €35M or 7% turnover</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><span class="framework-badge badge-nist">NIST CSF 2.0</span></td>
                <td>All organizations (voluntary)</td>
                <td>N/A (best practice)</td>
                <td>Reputational, contractual</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <h2 id="dora">2. DORA Compliance Checklist</h2>

    <p>The Digital Operational Resilience Act applies to financial entities operating in the EU and their critical
        ICT service providers.</p>

    <h3>Pillar 1: ICT Risk Management</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>ICT risk management framework
                documented and board-approved</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Dedicated ICT security function with
                clear responsibilities</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Business impact analysis covering all
                critical functions</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>ICT asset inventory maintained with
                classification</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Encryption standards for data at rest
                and in transit</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Access control with least privilege
                enforcement</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Vulnerability management program with
                SLAs</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Change management procedures
                documented</span></div>
    </div>

    <h3>Pillar 2: ICT Incident Management</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Incident classification scheme aligned
                with DORA definitions</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Major incident reporting to competent
                authority within 4 hours (initial)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Intermediate report within 72
                hours</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Final report within 1 month</span>
        </div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Root cause analysis process
                established</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Communication templates for regulatory
                notification</span></div>
    </div>

    <h3>Pillar 3: Digital Operational Resilience Testing</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Annual testing program
                documented</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Vulnerability assessments performed
                quarterly</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Penetration testing annually
                (minimum)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>TLPT (Threat-Led Penetration Testing)
                every 3 years for significant entities</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Scenario-based testing including cyber
                attack simulations</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Test results remediation
                tracking</span></div>
    </div>

    <h3>Pillar 4: ICT Third-Party Risk Management</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Register of all ICT third-party
                providers maintained</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Criticality assessment of each
                provider</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Contractual requirements include
                DORA-mandated clauses</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Exit strategies documented for
                critical providers</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Subcontracting chain visibility</span>
        </div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Annual due diligence reviews</span>
        </div>
    </div>

    <h3>Pillar 5: Information Sharing</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Participation in cyber threat
                intelligence sharing arrangements</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Internal procedures for sharing threat
                information with authorities</span></div>
    </div>

    <h2 id="euai">3. EU AI Act Compliance Checklist</h2>

    <p>The EU AI Act classifies AI systems by risk level. High-risk systems (HR, credit scoring, biometrics,
        critical infrastructure) face the most stringent requirements.</p>

    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Deadline Alert:</strong>
        High-risk AI system requirements apply from <strong>August 2, 2026</strong>. Organizations deploying AI in
        hiring, lending, law enforcement, or critical infrastructure must comply.
    </div>

    <h3>High-Risk AI System Requirements</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Risk management system established for
                AI lifecycle</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Training data quality requirements
                documented</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Technical documentation maintained
                (Annex IV)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Logging/audit trail capabilities
                enabled</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Transparency measures (users informed
                of AI use)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Human oversight mechanisms in
                place</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity
                measures</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Conformity assessment completed</span>
        </div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>CE marking applied (where
                required)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Registration in EU database</span>
        </div>
    </div>

    <h3>General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Model Obligations</h3>

    <p>If you deploy foundation models or LLMs:</p>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Technical documentation including
                training methodology</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Copyright compliance for training
                data</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Summary of training content
                published</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>EU AI Office cooperation
                procedures</span></div>
    </div>

    <h3>Prohibited AI Practices (Effective Feb 2025)</h3>

    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-ban"></i> Already Prohibited:</strong>
        <ul style="margin-top:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0;">
            <li>Social scoring by public authorities</li>
            <li>Real-time biometric identification in public spaces (with exceptions)</li>
            <li>Emotion recognition in workplace/education</li>
            <li>AI exploiting vulnerabilities (age, disability)</li>
            <li>Untargeted scraping for facial recognition databases</li>
        </ul>
    </div>

    <h2 id="nist">4. NIST CSF 2.0 Quick Reference</h2>

    <p>NIST CSF 2.0 introduced the GOVERN function, elevating cybersecurity risk to a board-level concern. The
        framework now has 6 core functions:</p>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Function</th>
                <th>Focus</th>
                <th>Key Activities</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:var(--accent-purple);font-weight:600;">GOVERN (New)</td>
                <td>Strategy & Oversight</td>
                <td>Risk appetite, roles, policies, supply chain</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:var(--accent-cyan);font-weight:600;">IDENTIFY</td>
                <td>Asset Management</td>
                <td>Inventory, BIA, risk assessment</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:var(--accent-green);font-weight:600;">PROTECT</td>
                <td>Safeguards</td>
                <td>Access control, training, data security</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:var(--accent-orange);font-weight:600;">DETECT</td>
                <td>Anomaly Discovery</td>
                <td>Monitoring, detection processes</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:var(--accent-red);font-weight:600;">RESPOND</td>
                <td>Incident Handling</td>
                <td>Response planning, communication</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td style="color:#64748b;font-weight:600;">RECOVER</td>
                <td>Restoration</td>
                <td>Recovery planning, improvements</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <h3>GOVERN Function Checklist (New in CSF 2.0)</h3>

    <div class="checklist">
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Organizational context documented
                (mission, stakeholders, legal)</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Risk management strategy with defined
                risk appetite</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Cybersecurity roles and
                responsibilities defined</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Policy framework established and
                communicated</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Board/executive oversight
                mechanisms</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Supply chain risk management
                program</span></div>
        <div class="checklist-item"><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> <span>Continuous improvement
                processes</span></div>
    </div>

    <h2 id="mapping">5. Control Mapping: One Effort, Three Frameworks</h2>

    <p>Many controls satisfy multiple frameworks. Efficient organizations implement once and document for each:</p>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Control Domain</th>
                <th>DORA</th>
                <th>EU AI Act</th>
                <th>NIST CSF 2.0</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Asset Inventory</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 8</td>
                <td>Annex IV</td>
                <td>ID.AM</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Risk Assessment</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 6</td>
                <td>Art. 9</td>
                <td>GV.RM, ID.RA</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Incident Response</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 17-19</td>
                <td>Art. 62</td>
                <td>RS.RP, RC.RP</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Third-Party Risk</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 28-30</td>
                <td>Art. 25</td>
                <td>GV.SC</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Access Control</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 9</td>
                <td>Art. 14</td>
                <td>PR.AA</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Logging/Monitoring</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 10</td>
                <td>Art. 12</td>
                <td>DE.CM</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Testing</strong></td>
                <td>Art. 24-27</td>
                <td>Art. 9</td>
                <td>ID.RA</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Efficiency Tip:</strong>
        Build your control library once using NIST CSF 2.0 as the baseline, then map to DORA and EU AI Act
        requirements. This reduces duplicate documentation by 40-60%.
    </div>

    <h2 id="audit">6. Audit Preparation Strategies</h2>

    <h3>30-Day Audit Readiness Plan</h3>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Week</th>
                <th>Focus Area</th>
                <th>Deliverables</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Week 1</strong></td>
                <td>Documentation Review</td>
                <td>Policy inventory, gap analysis, evidence index</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Week 2</strong></td>
                <td>Control Testing</td>
                <td>Internal control tests, remediation of gaps</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Week 3</strong></td>
                <td>Stakeholder Prep</td>
                <td>Interview scripts, RACI for audit queries</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Week 4</strong></td>
                <td>Mock Audit</td>
                <td>Dry-run walkthrough, final remediation</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <h3>Common Audit Findings to Avoid</h3>

    <ul>
        <li><strong>Stale documentation:</strong> Policies not updated within 12 months</li>
        <li><strong>Evidence gaps:</strong> Controls documented but no proof of execution</li>
        <li><strong>Incomplete vendor assessments:</strong> Critical providers without due diligence</li>
        <li><strong>Missing board reporting:</strong> No evidence of executive oversight</li>
        <li><strong>Testing gaps:</strong> No penetration test in >12 months</li>
    </ul>
